description: `grep -c . <file> 2>/dev/null||echo 0` produces a MULTI-LINE captured value whenever the target file exists but is EMPTY (0 matching lines): grep -c prints '0' to stdout but exits status 1 (no lines matched), so the `||echo 0` fallback ALSO fires inside the same command substitution, yielding the literal two-line string '0\n0'. This exact pattern occurs at verify-loops.sh:9, verify-loops.sh:15, and reddit-loop/loop.sh:21.
concreteFailureScenario: Before any real reddit->LM signup has ever occurred, attributed-signups.jsonl exists (touched by mkdir -p / initial state) but is empty, so SIGNUPS becomes the two-line string '0\n0'. loop.sh:35 then writes `echo "attributed_lm_signups: $SIGNUPS"` into STATE.md, silently inserting a stray extra '0' line into the state file. This is the exact 'grep -c returning multiline' bug class explicitly flagged for review, and it will corrupt any future parser that assumes one line per key in STATE.md.
